thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Detected spike in 5xx and p99 latency for region aws-ap-south-1 impacting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Auto-page -> @oncall_sre. Alert id: 1778888888. Dashboard: https://metrics.internal/redwood/alerts/1778888888

oncall_sre: Acknowledged. Kicking off triage. Quick asks: scope (Hosted vs Dedicated), vendor hits (auth/obs), customer-facing impact.

emily_ops: Data: Hosted API 5xx = 9.8% (was 0.3%), Dedicated pool ingress errors up ~6x. Heatmap shows controlplane->auth path and controlplane->obs-ingest failing with socket timeouts. Traces show long blocking auth token fetches at ~1.2s causing backlog and 502/503 to clients.

diego_platform: We're seeing repeated failures to sts.token.ap-south-1.example-auth.com and obs-ingest.partner.example.com. Vendor status pages show partial degraded performance in ap-south-1 for both providers. Vendor incidents: AUTH-V-617, OBS-V-221.

rachel_support: Support queue: ~12 customers opened tickets in last 8m. Notable: NimbusFin (enterprise) reporting transaction timeouts, KaptureShop on Dedicated reports 15% error rate on certain endpoints. Folks asking for ETA.

oncall_sre: Short mitigation plan: 1) divert new Hosted traffic from ap-south-1 to ap-southeast-1 via route policy; 2) scale up Dedicated standby capacity in us-east-1 and shift least-latency-tolerant customers; 3) enable auth token cache on controlplane (soft-TTL increase) to reduce STS call rate; 4) temporarily enable aggressive fail-fast/circuit-breaker on obs-ingest path so downstream doesn't block requests; 5) statuspage update. Who can run routing? @diego_platform can you?

diego_platform: Will apply route change. Using netroute tool:
```
netroute set --from ap-south-1 --scope hosted --to ap-southeast-1 --mode staged --initial 0.25
netroute set --from ap-south-1 --scope dedicated --to us-east-1 --mode staged --initial 0.2
```
Applying now. Estimated propagation 60-120s.

oncall_sre: Also flip token cache TTL for controlplane: increasing from 30s -> 300s to reduce STS QPS. Diego/rachel note: ensure we emit metric for token-staleness.

emily_ops: Pushed cache toggle to controlplane config: token_cache_ttl=300s (feature-flagged). Rolling restart small canary applied.

diego_platform: netroute reports first stage applied: hosted 25% diverted, dedicated 20%. Observability: partial drop in 5xx in diverted clusters.

vendor-bot: AUTH-V-617: "We are investigating increased request errors in ap-south-1 for token service. Root cause under investigation." OBS-V-221: "Ingest endpoint experiencing elevated latencies in ap-south-1; retries may surface as 500s to callers."

oncall_sre: Good. Also enable circuit breaker on obs path for 2xx-preferring flows: set cb_threshold=50ms_failed_requests=5 -> failfast 200ms. Diego can you push?

diego_platform: Pushing circuit-breaker rule to controlplane config-service now.

emily_ops: After staged diversion and token cache TTL bump: global 5xx fell from 9.8% -> 2.2% in 12m. Dedicated pool error volume decreased by ~65% for traffic routed away. Token-service calls reduced ~78% from baseline.

rachel_support: Customer comms draft: "We've detected elevated errors and latency in ap-south-1 due to third-party provider degradation. We've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; you may see reduced capacity or increased latency while we continue to monitor. We're proactively contacting impacted customers (NimbusFin, KaptureShop)." Approve to post?

oncall_sre: Post it and ping CSMs for NimbusFin + KaptureShop. Carter_sales, please take on the customer outreach for NimbusFin.

carter_sales: On it. Will send targeted note and offer to coordinate retries/backoff on their side.

vendor-bot: AUTH-V-617 update: "Partial recovery observed; error rate decreasing but increased latency persists. Monitoring. Incident ETA unknown." OBS-V-221 update: "We have applied an internal fix in ap-south-1; ingestion is trending healthier."

emily_ops: Monitoring tail latency: p99 still elevated ~700ms vs baseline 120ms for controlplane in ap-south-1, but user-facing error rates stabilized. Recommend keeping staged routing for 30 more minutes then slowly drift back if vendors confirm.

oncall_sre: Agree. Handoff timeline: I need to step out in 30m. I will hand to diego_platform at 1778889080. Diego, please own until full recovery and vendor clear. Action items for post-incident: RCA, vendor correlation, improve token cache strategy, implement proactive token caching per-tenant for high QPS accounts, and add playbook step to auto-drift dedicated pools on third-party auth failure.

diego_platform: Taking the handoff. I'll continue monitoring and coordinate rollback once vendors report healthy.

oncall_sre: Status change -> mitigate (partial) at 1778889100. Next update required by 1778889400. Good job team.

rachel_support: Posted status page update and outbound emails to impacted customers. No new high-severity tickets in the last 10m.

emily_ops: Collecting traces/troubleshooting artifacts and saving to incident artifacts: s3://incidents/1778888888/traces.tar.gz. Will attach to postmortem.

diego_platform: Leaving sticky notes: runbook update to include token cache TTL emergency toggle, add monitoring for vendor token latency >300ms as a trigger for automated routing.

oncall_sre: Closing active pager. Will review RCA draft tomorrow. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
